not recorded on the page this object was extracted from

The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they should have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason.

The registered primary of both trials is a median percent change from baseline to Week 12 in fasting serum triglycerides -- that wording is on both registrations. This pool is a mean difference. In populations selected for triglycerides above 500 mg/dL (marine) and above 200 mg/dL (anchor) the mean and the median diverge by construction, so this pooled value answers a question neither trial asked. The estimate is not changed here: correcting a summary statistic changes what the published number means and that is a content decision.

Both trials registered three arms -- placebo, AMR101 2 g/day and AMR101 4 g/day. This object records two. A dose arm was selected and the selection is recorded nowhere. A review that selects among registered options without recording the selection has made an analytic decision that cannot be audited from its own output.

Abstract

Question. In adults with hypertriglyceridemia, does AMR101 (ethyl icosapentate) - 4 g/day compared with placebo affect difference between amr101 (ethyl icosapentate) and placebo treatment groups in triglyceride lowering effect?1

Methods. eligibility was not recorded on the page this object was extracted from; estimates were pooled under a random-effects with the REML estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials); and certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.2

Results. Difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering Effect: mean difference -25.8 (-36.8 to -14.8) across 2 trials; 1 of these pooled outcome(s) carries a stated qualification -- a referral or a recorded finding -- given in full in Results and not reproduced here; the trials agreed loosely (I-squared 64.2%); and certainty of the evidence was very low.3

Results

The pooled mean difference for difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering Effect was -25.8 (-36.8 to -14.8) across 2 trials, against not recorded on the page this object was extracted from.1

Noted on this pool. The registered primary of both trials is a median percent change from baseline to Week 12 in fasting serum triglycerides -- that wording is on both registrations. This pool is a mean difference. In populations selected for triglycerides above 500 mg/dL (marine) and above 200 mg/dL (anchor) the mean and the median diverge by construction, so this pooled value answers a question neither trial asked. The estimate is not changed here: correcting a summary statistic changes what the published number means and that is a content decision. Both trials registered three arms -- placebo, AMR101 2 g/day and AMR101 4 g/day. This object records two. A dose arm was selected and the selection is recorded nowhere. A review that selects among registered options without recording the selection has made an analytic decision that cannot be audited from its own output.2

The trials' results were loosely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 64.2%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 43.2, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 2.79, on degrees of freedom 1. not recorded on the page this object was extracted from3

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they should have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.4

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.5

Risk of bias in the included results

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials). The unit of assessment is a result1

A domain that cannot be judged from the sources read is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect. Overall is capped at SOME_CONCERNS wherever a domain is NO_INFORMATION.2

A second, independent assessment was obtained from: gpt-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`3

The assessment above was made by: Claude Opus 5 (anthropic family) -- the assessment above4

How the second assessor was asked: Blind, from scripts/second_assessor_prompt.py, which assembles the prompt from an ALLOW-LIST of registry-sourced factual fields and refuses to send it if any RoB 2 verdict word appears in the assembled text. The second assessor was not shown this assessment and was not asked whether it agreed. It was given this project's NO_INFORMATION-never-LOW rule so the comparison measures judgement rather than house dialect.5

The disagreement rate, reported as disagreement because agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing: 6 of 12 judgements -- 50.0%. Reported as disagreement: agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing.6

Where they disagree, by domain: D1 2 of 2 disagree, D2 0 of 2 disagree, D3 0 of 2 disagree, D4 1 of 2 disagree, D5 2 of 2 disagree and overall 1 of 2 disagree.7

That rate was measured before this review's D1 judgements moved. It is left as measured: On 2026-08-21 this review's D1 judgements moved from LOW to NO_INFORMATION on the RoB 2 guidance -- the position assessor 2 had taken. The rate above was measured before that and is left exactly as measured: it is a published number, it is the record of what a blind second assessor said, and it is the reason the guidance was re-read. Editing it would delete the evidence that the change was warranted. This is the same computation re-run on the object as it now stands, so both are visible and neither is silently corrected.8

Re-run on the object as it now stands: 4 of 12 judgements -- 33.3%. By domain: D1 0 of 2 disagree, D2 0 of 2 disagree, D3 0 of 2 disagree, D4 1 of 2 disagree, D5 2 of 2 disagree and overall 1 of 2 disagree.9

2 D1 judgement(s) on this topic moved. Any D1 disagreement that remains is one where this assessment said SOME_CONCERNS rather than LOW -- assessor 2 said NO_INFORMATION there too, and the guidance applied here speaks to LOW, not to SOME_CONCERNS. So a claim that 'the D1 disagreement is resolved' would be false wherever those two numbers differ, which is why the count is re-run per topic instead of asserted once.10

D1 now agrees with assessor 2 on every compared result.11

Class 94 records assessor 2 saying NO_INFORMATION on D1/D2/D3 `100 of 100`. Measured across all 23 topics now stored that is 239 of 243, and all four exceptions are D1=SOME_CONCERNS on `agyw-hiv-prep-review` and `cab-prep-hiv-review` -- two of the three topics asked under the earlier prompt build, the one whose reply ids are bare NCTs. Under that build it is 4 of 6; under the later build 0 of 75. The 100% was measured on the later build's topics. The two-defaults mechanism stands; its universality does not, and what varies with it is the prompt.12

Every disagreement, named: NCT01047501 on Difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering Effect D1: assessor 1 LOW, assessor 2 NO_INFORMATION; NCT01047501 on Difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering Effect D4: assessor 1 LOW, assessor 2 SOME_CONCERNS; NCT01047501 on Difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering Effect D5: assessor 1 SOME_CONCERNS, assessor 2 LOW; NCT01047683 on Difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering Effect D1: assessor 1 LOW, assessor 2 NO_INFORMATION; NCT01047683 on Difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering Effect D5: assessor 1 SOME_CONCERNS, assessor 2 LOW; NCT01047683 on Difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering Effect overall: assessor 1 SOME_CONCERNS, assessor 2 NO_INFORMATION.13

Risk of bias was assessed independently a second time by GPT-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`, blind to this assessment and given the same registry facts. 6 of 12 judgements -- 50.0%. Reported as disagreement: agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing. By domain: D1 2 of 2 disagree, D2 0 of 2 disagree, D3 0 of 2 disagree, D4 1 of 2 disagree, D5 2 of 2 disagree, overall 1 of 2 disagree. Recounted after this review's D1 judgements moved: 4 of 12 judgements -- 33.3%.14

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons..1

No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect or a dose-response gradient applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here.2

Certainty VERY_LOW. The risk-of-bias domain reads the per-result RoB 2 assessments made 2026-08-20 and named above, not a topic-level summary; indirectness reads the estimand findings recorded on this pool.3

Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: D5 on 2 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.4

Certainty of the evidence, by outcome, with every rating step5
OutcomeCertaintykStarted atRating steps
difference Between AMR101 (Ethyl Icosapentate) and Placebo Treatment Groups in Triglyceride Lowering EffectVERY_LOW2HIGHrisk of bias: HIGH to MODERATE, down 1 level(s) -- both results are SOME_CONCERNS and the driver is not empagliflozin's. D5 is SOME_CONCERNS in its own right: the registered primary is a median percent change and this pool is a mean difference, and both trials registered three arms where the object records two. D2 and D3 are additionally NO_INFORMATION -- and D3 here is a live threat rather than a formality, because a week-12 laboratory value is missing when a participant leaves, where a time-to-event result absorbs the same withdrawal by censoring. (rating: serious); inconsistency: MODERATE to LOW, down 1 level(s) -- I-squared is 64.2% with tau-squared 43.19 over k=2. Handbook 10.10.2 warns against reading I-squared mechanically, and at this k the estimate is imprecise -- but the point estimates themselves differ materially and the direction of the finding does not rest on the statistic alone. (rating: serious); indirectness: LOW to VERY_LOW, down 1 level(s) -- the pooled quantity is not the registered quantity. Both registrations describe the primary as a median percent change from baseline to week 12 in fasting serum triglycerides; this pool is a mean difference. In populations selected on a triglyceride threshold -- above 500 mg/dL in marine, above 200 in anchor -- the mean and the median diverge by construction, which is precisely why a trialist reports a median. The pool therefore answers a question neither trial asked, and that is an indirectness fact, not a footnote. Compounded by a dose arm selected from three registered arms with the selection recorded nowhere. (rating: serious); imprecision: down 1 level(s) -- k=2, and the interval -36.84 to -14.84 spans a 22-point range on a percentage change. Two trials of 229 and 702 participants do not meet an optimal information size for an effect reported as a percentage of a skewed baseline. Handbook 15.6.2. (rating: serious); publication bias: not rated down -- not assessed rather than assessed as ABSENT. Funnel-plot asymmetry and its tests are uninformative below about ten studies -- Handbook 13.3.5.4 -- and these pools carry two or three. 'Undetected' here means nobody looked with an instrument that could see, not that publication bias is unlikely. Not rated down, because rating down on an unmeasurable domain would invent a defect. (rating: undetected)

Discussion

[Draft] The pooled MD is -25.84 (95% CI -36.84 to -14.84) over 2 trials. Certainty is rated VERY_LOW. Every contributing interval excludes no effect. Whether a change of that magnitude is clinically meaningful in this population is the author's judgement: no field on this object records a threshold of importance, and none is assumed here.1

[Draft] Across 2 trials, tau-squared 43.1921; every trial interval excludes no effect. Whether that degree of disagreement matters clinically -- whether the trials are answering the same question in the same patients -- is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] This review pools -25.84 (95% CI -36.84 to -14.84) over 2 trials. The appraised synthesis pooled an outcome not recorded here. Which trials that synthesis carries: Marine keyed to NCT01047683 and anchor to NCT01047501, each carrying the registry's own posted primary-outcome title, before any count was compared. Why the two results differ -- whether by population, outcome definition, model or included set -- is the author's judgement.3

[Draft] The evidence base is 2 trials, assessed for risk of bias as SOME_CONCERNS on 2 result(s). GRADE certainty is VERY_LOW. Whether that is enough to answer the question depends on the decision the answer is for, which is not stated on this object, and is the author's judgement.4

[Draft] primary trials. No bibliographic search for primary trials was run. The 2 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on the dates recorded on each entry; The basis on which this object was verified is not recorded. What this object does not claim is not recorded. The bar this object had to clear is not recorded.. Whether that is broad enough for the claim this review makes is the author's judgement.5

[Draft] Certainty was not rated down on any GRADE domain. What further evidence would change the conclusion is a judgement about a trial nobody has run, and is the author's.6

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities; query, counts and a per-record decision in ssot/icosapent-lipid-auto-full-review/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json. 35 matched, 20 retrieved, 4 appraised, 31 not read. No included-study table was read: trial sets are inferred from abstract text and stated scope.1

This review was compared against 2 published synthesis(es); the denominator is stated because a comparison against an unstated number of reviews is not a comparison.2

On what basis their trial set is known: Marine keyed to NCT01047683 and anchor to NCT01047501, each carrying the registry's own posted primary-outcome title, before any count was compared.3

Where our result differs from theirs: By dose, species and population -- not by disagreement. The published figures average across omega-3 species and the whole dose range; this review is purified EPA at the top of that range in the population where the effect is largest. Their own dose-dependence predicts the direction of the gap, and nothing available predicts its size. No identified synthesis pools these two trials, so none of them is an independent check on this estimate.4
